## 3. Identity: seat → desk, install → room, rooms → floor

### 3.1 The keys, and why they are the only ones

| Rendered thing | Key | Source | Stability |
|---|---|---|---|
| **desk** | `(install_id, seat_id)` | [D2 § 8.2.1](FLEET-STATE.md#821-the-seat-state-object), which carries both on every seat object and every delta, bounded at 32 B and 48 B | D1's identity-stability rule: both are **config-file resident** and "survive session restarts, `/clear`, reboots, host renames, and harness upgrades" ([D1 § 3.1](EVENT-SCHEMA.md#31-the-seat-config-file)). They change only when a human edits the file, which is a deliberate re-identification of the desk |
| **room** | `install_id` | the snapshot's `installs[].install_id`, and the `install_id` every message on the stream carries ([D2 § 8.3](FLEET-STATE.md#83-the-websocket-delta-feed)) | same file, same rule |
| **floor** | its **key** — the lexically least `install_id` among the floor's rooms ([§ 4.6](#46-the-building-layout)), **derived and never authored**. ⚠ A floor's **label** ([§ 4.6](#46-the-building-layout), card#9273) is **not this column**: it is a rendered name, nothing routes, sorts or matches on it, and editing it moves no key | the **building layout**, authored by the operator and read by nobody on the write side; an install the layout does not place is a floor of its own, keyed by itself. A floor key is always the `install_id` of one of the floor's own rooms, so it is stable in exactly the way the row above is | the layout is authored in the admin console and served by [D2 § 8.7](FLEET-STATE.md#87-the-building-surface--the-layout-the-room-maps-and-the-message-that-says-one-changed) (card#9208's reversal, 2026-09-12 — it was a deploy-time artifact until then); a floor changes when an operator composes one, which is a deliberate act with a revision behind it ([D2 § 6.11](FLEET-STATE.md#611-the-authored-building-store--room-maps-the-layout-and-their-revisions)), and its key moves only when a room that sorts below it is added — the old key still resolves ([§ 4.4](#44-routes-and-what-each-one-fetches)) |
| **character identity** (which sprite a seat gets) | `(install_id, seat_id)` — and, for the **body alone**, the seat object's `character.species` ([D2 § 8.2.1](FLEET-STATE.md#821-the-seat-state-object), card#12443) | the **species** is allocated by D2 once, in the transaction that creates the seat, unique among live seats while the list allows ([D2 § 6.13](FLEET-STATE.md#613-the-character-allocation--one-species-per-seat-allocated-at-creation-and-kept-for-life)), and delivered on every seat object; **every other field** — colourway, face, girth, what it wears — is the creature generator's, seeded from the key ([§ 10.2](#102-characters-original-creatures-drawn-by-code), [§ 10.4](#104-the-art-direction-as-a-specification)) | a seat looks the same on every reload and on every browser: its body because D2 stores it and never moves it, the rest because the seed is the identity and not a random draw. ⚠ Until card#12443 the body was the key's own draw too, and the operator saw two seats of one floor wear one body ([D2 § 6.13](FLEET-STATE.md#613-the-character-allocation--one-species-per-seat-allocated-at-creation-and-kept-for-life)'s evidence): *the same on every browser* is a property a pure function gives for free, and *unlike every other seat* is one it cannot |

⭐ **A ROOM IS AN INSTALL; A FLOOR IS AN OPERATOR-COMPOSED SET OF ROOMS — operator ruling, 2026-09-11
(card#9267), which closed [§ 14](#14-open-questions-for-the-review-loop) item 6 and is the reason this
table has two rows where it had one.** The **coordination** unit — who shares a PM, the stream's per-subscriber
filter key and an ACL attachment point — is `install_id` and did not move; the **display** unit — what is drawn on one
screen — is the floor. Until that ruling both were `install_id`, which is why one solo agent was
forced to be a whole floor. [§ 4.6](#46-the-building-layout) owns the layout that composes them, and
everything D1 and D2 key on `install_id` is untouched by it.

⚠ **Where the rest of this document says *floor* of a thing keyed by `install_id` — a map file, a
slot set, the reach of a round — it means the ROOM, and this table is the one place the
two are told apart.** Every section the ruling made literally **false** was amended with it, and
each of those sites carries a ⚠ or ⭐ note naming **card#9267** — so the amended set is read out of
the document (`grep -n 'card#9267'`) rather than listed here, because a list of section numbers is
a second home for a set the document already states and would go stale at the next one found. It
went stale inside the amending card itself, which is why it is a derivation and not a list.

⚠ **And *room* now carries a SECOND noun, which is the one this table did not mint: the older name
for the drawn interior — [§ 4.2](#42-the-floor)'s and [A17](#62-the-animation-table--the-closed-set)'s
room render is the drawn interior of a floor and is not this table's room.** One is a key and one is
a picture: the room render is drawn **once per floor** ([§ 4.2](#42-the-floor)) however many rooms
the layout composes onto it, so a later section that has the room *set*, *frozen* or *advancing*, or
that gives it elements, warmth or a corner, is naming that picture and never an install — which is
why those sites are not amended and are not defects. **The sweep of both nouns was done in
card#9267 itself and is not deferred**: every occurrence of *room* in this document was read against
both senses, every site where a container reading was available and wrong was amended and carries
the marker, and what is left is the drawn place — a sentence no install fits.

**What may never key a desk**, each named because it is a plausible mistake: `session_id` (it changes
on every `/clear` — D1 § 3.2), the harness or model label, the reporter version, the seat's position in
the snapshot array, arrival order, a browser-local id, or anything derived from hostname, cwd or
username (D1 § 3.4 is a 30-day outage caused by exactly that class of key). A desk keyed on any of
them re-identifies itself under the ordinary operation of the seat it draws.

### 3.2 The desk slot function

A **room's** map declares its desk slots, and the slot function runs **per room**. The client assigns
seats to slots by a **pure function of the rendered seat set**, so two browsers, two reloads and two
server restarts agree without a stored position and without a server field.

⚠ **This section said *floor* until card#9267's ruling, and the word had to move rather than be left
to read loosely.** A floor is now N rooms ([§ 4.6](#46-the-building-layout)), so *the floor's seats*
would pool two installs' seats into one slot set — and then composing a second room onto a floor
would re-hash every desk in the first, which is the precise cost this section rejects sorted order
for two paragraphs below. Per room, a seat's slot is a function of `(install_id, seat_id)` and that
room's own `S`, so **rearranging the building moves no desk inside any room.** A floor is its rooms'
slot sets drawn on one screen; the function is layout-agnostic and does not know which.

```
  h(seat)  = FNV-1a-32( install_id + "/" + seat_id )      # offset basis 2166136261, prime 16777619,
                                                          # over the UTF-8 bytes; both ids are ASCII
                                                          # by D1 § 3.1's slug patterns
  S        = the number of slots the ROOM's map declares
  (k, R)   = (index after the id sort, role) of the one `desks` object carrying
             `reserved_for` (§ 10.3), else NONE
  eligible = { seat in room : seat.protocol_agent_role === R }   # strings only: null equals nothing
  holder   = the single member of eligible when |eligible| == 1, else NONE
  taken    = { k } if k is not NONE                        # reserved, held or not
  slot(holder) = k                                         # if holder is not NONE
  order    = the room's seats other than holder, ascending by (h, seat_id)
                                                          # total: seat_id is unique within an install
  for seat in order:
      for i in 0 … S-1:
          if slot ((h + i) mod S) is not taken -> take it, stop
      # no free slot: the overflow rule below
```

**The reserved desk is a slot taken before the loop** (card#11144). A map may reserve one desk for a
role ([§ 10.3](#103-the-floor-map)'s `reserved_for`); the room's one seat whose relayed
`protocol_agent_role` ([D1 § 3.1](EVENT-SCHEMA.md#31-the-seat-config-file)) equals it, compared as
strings, sits there, and the client knows no role by name — only the equality. **With nobody eligible
the desk stays empty and reserved** (the operator's ruling Q3 A), and **with two or more eligible
nobody sits there** (Q4 A): each hashes as an ordinary seat and [§ 9](#9-failure-paths-and-their-observables)
F22's notice names them. Either way the loop never hands the desk out — a hash landing on it probes
on exactly as one landing on a held desk does, so the ring stays `S` desks wide and no other seat's
hash changes because a desk is reserved.

| Case | What happens | Who moves | Animation / narration |
|---|---|---|---|
| reserved, nobody eligible | the desk is empty and reserved; the others hash with `k` taken | nobody | the plain floor at the desk; [§ 5.5](#55-the-clients-own-narration)'s *reserved for `pm` (id 3) — no seat holds that role* |
| a seat's first appearance with the role | [§ 3.4](#34-a-new-seats-first-appearance)'s first-appearance row | the seat, and at most its chain | [A1](#62-the-animation-table--the-closed-set) (or an insert) at its hash slot, then [A16](#62-the-animation-table--the-closed-set) to the reserved desk |
| the holder retires | [A13](#62-the-animation-table--the-closed-set); `k` stays empty and reserved | nobody ([§ 3.5](#35-retirement-and-the-only-removal)) | A13 only |
| a relayed role changes on a delta | the seat moves between its hash slot and `k`; the chain through the slot it leaves or takes re-probes | that seat, and at most its chain | A16, its `cause` the delta's `state_version` |
| two eligible seats (Q4 A) | the desk seats nobody; both hash as ordinary seats; the incumbent walks out and may displace one | the incumbent, and at most its chain | A16 (its `cause` the arriving seat's key, or the delta that made the second seat eligible); [§ 9](#9-failure-paths-and-their-observables) F22's notice |
| a handover | F22 while both are present: the incumbent walks out; on the old one's retirement the new one walks in. Retiring the old one first avoids the walk-out | both, in turn | A16, then A13 and A16 |
| no reservation on the map | the function above with `k` NONE — every seat hashes | — | — |
| a save adds or removes the reservation | a layout act; the chain through `k` re-probes | at most that chain | none ([decision 29](#13-decisions-taken-revisable-at-review)) |
| ordinary seats past `S − 1` | the overflow row below; [§ 9](#9-failure-paths-and-their-observables) F13 counts them against the `S − 1` desks left | — | — |

**Worked assignment — the shipped default map, S = 6, which is the map the `aimla` room renders
until an operator authors one.** The map is **served at runtime** ([D2 § 8.7](FLEET-STATE.md#87-the-building-surface--the-layout-the-room-maps-and-the-message-that-says-one-changed)), and
[§ 10.3](#103-the-floor-map) is where the default lives — it is in the tree since card#9269 — and what holds `S` to it. Every value below is re-derived by
`tools/design/verify-floor.py` from the function above, not transcribed:

| Seat | `h` | `h mod 6` | Probes | Slot |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aimla/aimla-review` | 185683291 | 1 | 0 | **1** |
| `aimla/aimla-impl-1` | 671323131 | 3 | 0 | **3** |
| `aimla/aimla-impl-2` | 688100750 | 2 | 2 | **4** |
| `aimla/aimla-pm` | 2865560748 | 0 | role | **2** |

The default reserves its desk id 3 — index **2** after the id sort — for `pm`
([§ 10.3](#103-the-floor-map)), and `aimla-pm` is the room's one seat relaying `pm`, so it sits there
by its role and its Probes cell reads `role`: it never entered the loop. `aimla-impl-2`'s hash slot
**is** the reserved desk, so it probes 2 → 3 → 4 — the reserved desk skipped exactly as a held one is.

**Why a hash and not the obvious alternatives.** Sorting seats by `seat_id` into slots 1…N is simpler
and is rejected: inserting `aimla-alpha` would shift **every** later desk by one, so provisioning one
seat rearranges the whole office and every operator's spatial memory of it. Assigning in arrival order
is rejected for the opposite reason — it is not a function of the rendered set at all, so two browsers
disagree and a reload moves the furniture. A server-assigned position would be a new field, which
[§ 1.2](#12-non-goals--stated-so-an-implementer-cannot-widen-scope-in-good-faith) forbids this document
from minting.

**Overflow: a seat is never dropped.** If the room's seat count exceeds `S`, the seats with no slot
are rendered in an explicitly labelled **overflow row** below the floor, its label reading
***Overflow — seats past the map's desks*** (ratified by the operator on card#7342, 2026-09-25) — same desk, same render, same
drill-down — and the floor shows a persistent notice reading *floor map is short N desks*. A silent
drop would be a seat that exists and is invisible, which is the same lie as an empty office and is
worse for being local. On a floor of several rooms ([§ 4.6](#46-the-building-layout)) the row is still the
**floor's** — one band below the composed floor — and the notice is rendered **once per short room,
as *floor map is short N desks — `install_id`***, the bare form being a one-room floor's whose single
map needs no naming: a floor now has N maps, and *which map is short* is the question the notice
exists to answer (card#9292). A floor plan changes no seat's fate here: a room
drawn *for PM+3impl* holds its map's `S` desks and a seat past them is this row, planned or not.
Map authors should size `S` above the install's planned seat count; the
shipped default declares 6, because most floors hold six agents or fewer (the operator's ruling of
2026-10-01, card#11045, which sized the default for six so its room is legible at fit in a laptop
window) — a PM at its reserved desk and five others (card#11144); for the `aimla` room's four seats,
the PM among them, that leaves two desks free
([`docs/PLAN.md § 5`](../PLAN.md#5-deployment): aimla's four seats first, then a Windows validation seat,
then others as they opt in). **A seventh agent is this row and its notice**, and that notice is the
prompt to author a map with more desks: the bench is the designed answer to growth, not an accident.

### 3.3 Collision, displacement, and why a desk move is itself an event

Two seats of one install can hash to one slot. The chain resolves by the `(h, seat_id)` order above,
which means an **arriving seat can displace an incumbent** — deterministically, and only when it sorts
lower in the chain.

**Worked collision.** On the shipped default above — the `aimla` room's map — provisioning `aimla-mac-1` (h = 214254736,
h mod 6 = **4**) collides with `aimla-impl-2` (h = 688100750, slot 4). 214254736 < 688100750, so
`aimla-mac-1` takes slot 4 and `aimla-impl-2` probes to slot **5**. Every other desk is untouched — the
holder included: an arrival never displaces the reserved desk. (`aimla-impl-4`, h mod 6 = 0, lands on
the PM's free hash slot and moves nobody.)

This is a real cost and it is paid deliberately: incumbent-stability would require tenure, tenure would
require a `first_seen` the wire does not carry, and inventing one is what
[§ 1.2](#12-non-goals--stated-so-an-implementer-cannot-widen-scope-in-good-faith) forbids. Three things
make the cost bounded and honest:

1. **A displacement has a cause and is rendered as one.** The move is animation row
   [A16](#62-the-animation-table--the-closed-set), driven by the arrival of a seat in the rendered set —
   a real event, not a re-layout. The displaced character walks to the new desk; under reduced motion
   the desk simply appears in its new place on the next render.
2. **It is bounded to the collision chain.** No seat outside the chain moves, and
   [AT-D3-3](#at-d3-3-identity-is-stable-across-a-restart) asserts exactly that against the fixture
   above.
3. **The frequency is stated, not hoped.** The chance that an arriving seat collides is `N/S`, where
   `N` counts the held-or-reserved slots — the reserved desk counts as held whether or not anyone
   holds it ([§ 3.2](#32-the-desk-slot-function)); on the
   shipped default as the `aimla` room renders it (N = 4, S = 6) that is **2 in 3**, and it displaces only when it also sorts lower —
   so a map author who wants displacement rarer raises `S`, and the formula says by how much. ⚠ **That is
   twice the twelve-desk default's 1 in 3, and it is the price of the six-desk room** (card#11045): a fifth
   `aimla` seat is more likely than not to land on a held slot, and when it sorts lower it moves one desk
   ([A16](#62-the-animation-table--the-closed-set)) — bounded, animated and caused, as above.

**Two seats claiming one identity is not a case, and no branch is built for it.** A token binds exactly
one `(install_id, seat_id)` ([D1 § 3.1](EVENT-SCHEMA.md#31-the-seat-config-file),
[D1 § 3.3](EVENT-SCHEMA.md#33-authentication-and-the-identity-binding-rule)), so duplicate identity is
caught at token-issue time and cannot reach the wire. A client-side de-duplication branch would be a
branch no input can select — the defect D1 and D2 both name and delete.

### 3.4 A new seat's first appearance

A seat exists on the floor from the moment it is provisioned, because
[D2 § 4.5](FLEET-STATE.md#45-link-states) rule 1 gives a seat that has never reported
`link_state: "offline"`, and [D2 § 4.3](FLEET-STATE.md#43-the-derivation-function) rule 5 gives it
`activity_state: "unknown"` / `no_data_yet`. `render_state` collapses to **`offline`**.

| Moment | What the floor shows | Driven by |
|---|---|---|
| provisioned, never reported | the desk, the nameplate, **no character** — an empty chair and the label *no data yet* | `render_state: "offline"`, `unknown_reason: "no_data_yet"` — and `delivery.last_receipt_at: null` is the upstream **input** D2 § 4.5 rule 1 mints those from, **`named-not-rendered`** here ([§ 2.4](#24-the-clock-and-every-age-on-the-page)) |
| first batch lands | the character **steps out of the elevator**, walks to its desk and sits ([A1](#62-the-animation-table--the-closed-set)) | the delta whose `changed[]` carries `render_state`, leaving `stale` or `offline` for a member that draws a character ([§ 6.2](#62-the-animation-table--the-closed-set)'s walk note item 1) |
| first `tool.start` | the working loop begins ([A3](#62-the-animation-table--the-closed-set)) | `render_state: "working"` |
| the seat was inserted by [§ 2.3](#23-membership-a-seat-or-an-install-the-client-does-not-hold)'s fetch | the desk appears **without** an arrival animation, and the client's event log records *seat added to the floor* | an insert is not a state change; the arrival animation is reserved for a seat leaving `stale` or `offline` for a member that draws a character ([§ 6.2](#62-the-animation-table--the-closed-set)'s walk note item 1), which is a claim the wire actually made |
| the seat relays the role its room's map reserves a desk for ([§ 3.2](#32-the-desk-slot-function), card#11144) | **first at its hash slot**, by the row above that applies — [A1](#62-the-animation-table--the-closed-set) for a client holding the seat from a snapshot, the insert's appearance with no animation for a client that connected before it was provisioned — **then a walk to the reserved desk** ([A16](#62-the-animation-table--the-closed-set)), and the chain through the slot it left re-probes | a provisioned seat renders `offline` with `protocol_agent_role: null` before it reports, and the reporter's first pass drains before it heartbeats, so the role arrives on a later delta than the one that took the seat out of `offline`. That delta is A16's `cause` ([§ 11](#11-acceptance-tests)); landing while the A1 walk is in flight, it cancels that walk ([§ 6.2](#62-the-animation-table--the-closed-set)'s walk note item 6), and the seat appears seated at the reserved desk |

The distinction in the last row is the honesty principle applied to the one edge where an implementer
would naturally reach for the nicer effect: *a desk appearing because the client had not fetched it yet*
and *a seat coming online* are different facts, and only the second one happened to the seat.

### 3.5 Retirement, and the only removal

Retirement is an operator act ([D2 § 4.10](FLEET-STATE.md#410-retirement-is-a-rendered-state)) and it
is an **announcement** — so the desk it names **goes immediately**, on the message that announces it.

⛔ **REVERSED BY OPERATOR RULING — card#9078, 2026-09-09 — and this section IS the reversal.** Until
then it read *"rendered, not disappeared"*: the desk stayed in its slot, cleared and stamped
`retired`, until D2's read filter dropped the seat fourteen days later. The operator, verbatim:
*"An absence and removal are very obviously different because if an agent is not reporting, it is
assumed to be an absence. A removal is a deliberate action by the operator. When an agent is
removed, its seat and desk should go away immediately."*

⚠ **The argument this document made for the lingering desk is recorded rather than deleted, because
it is the one a maintainer will re-derive.** It was that the cleared desk kept *"we removed it"*
distinguishable from *"it went quiet"*. It is false on [§ 7.1](#71-the-render-per-state)'s own render
table: a seat that goes quiet is **visibly present and degraded** — `stale` at 300 s, `offline` at
900 s, each with a *no data since* label — so a desk that is simply **gone** is maximally different
from it. The nameplate was never doing the disambiguating work claimed for it.

| Fact | Render |
|---|---|
| the `seat.retired` message | **the desk is removed from the floor** ([A13](#62-the-animation-table--the-closed-set)), and one line goes into the client's event log ([§ 5.5](#55-the-clients-own-narration)) naming the seat, the **reason** and the **time** — the two its payload carries ([D2 § 8.3](FLEET-STATE.md#83-the-websocket-delta-feed): `install_id`, `seat_id`, `reason`, `at`, and **no `by`**). That log line is now the whole of what this floor says about a retirement, and it is what makes the removal a removal rather than a disappearance |
| the delta carrying `render_state: "retired"` | the same removal, from the other of the two announcements D2 publishes in one transaction. The client may receive either first and **both are idempotent** ([§ 2.5](#25-what-re-renders-and-when)); the second one arrives about a desk that is already gone and changes nothing. ⛔ It is the **announcement** that removes, never the seat's absence from anything ([§ 2.3](#23-membership-a-seat-or-an-install-the-client-does-not-hold)) |
| `retired.at` / `.by` / `.reason` | **not rendered on this floor at all.** The record does not go with the desk — it **moves**: the admin console's agent module is its home, where it is queryable, bounded by no window, and consumes no slot on a floor whose slot count is finite ([D2 § 4.10](FLEET-STATE.md#410-retirement-is-a-rendered-state)). ⛔ The client draws **no** retirement plate, and must not assemble one from the removal log line: `by` is not on the wire at the moment of the announcement, so a plate that named an operator would name one the wire never sent ([§ 5.4](#54-what-is-never-rendered)) |
| `link_state` / `activity_state` underneath | nothing on this floor renders them once the desk is gone — the drill-down goes with the desk. D2 keeps deriving them ([D2 § 4.10](FLEET-STATE.md#410-retirement-is-a-rendered-state)) and its own read surfaces stop serving the seat at `retired_at`, so this client cannot fetch what a removed seat was doing; the console above is where that question is asked |
| the seat's absence from the next snapshot | **nothing happens — the desk left on the announcement**, and a population that no longer lists the seat agrees with a floor that no longer draws it. [§ 2.3](#23-membership-a-seat-or-an-install-the-client-does-not-hold)'s last row remains as the **backstop** for the one client this cannot reach: one that was disconnected when the announcement went out |
| the reserved desk's holder ([§ 3.2](#32-the-desk-slot-function), card#11144) | its desk is removed like any other, and **the reserved desk stays empty and reserved** — taken before the probe loop whether or not anyone holds it, so the holder's retirement **moves nobody** and writes no [A16](#62-the-animation-table--the-closed-set) |
| the desks that shared its collision chain | they **re-probe**, because [§ 3.2](#32-the-desk-slot-function)'s assignment is a pure function of the **rendered seat set** and that set just changed. The move is [A16](#62-the-animation-table--the-closed-set) — a desk move is an event and is animated as one — and it is bounded to the chain, exactly as an arrival's displacement is ([§ 3.3](#33-collision-displacement-and-why-a-desk-move-is-itself-an-event)). ⚠ **This is a cost the ruling adds, stated here rather than discovered on a floor:** a retirement can move one other desk. Holding the departed seat's slot to avoid it would be a stored position — which [§ 1.2](#12-non-goals--stated-so-an-implementer-cannot-widen-scope-in-good-faith) forbids this document from minting — and would make the assignment depend on history instead of on the set |

**A desk still never vanishes because data went missing.** The rule
[D2 § 4.5](FLEET-STATE.md#45-link-states) states, and
[§ 2.3](#23-membership-a-seat-or-an-install-the-client-does-not-hold)'s last row implements, is that a
seat is never removed from an **absence**: not from a delta, not from a poll, not from a seat
fetch's one object, not from silence, not from a timeout. **That is untouched by this ruling and is the
whole of what the ruling leaves standing** — what changed is that an *announcement* now removes, and
an announcement is the opposite of an absence: a message, from the one act that writes it, carrying
an author and a reason.
[AT-D2-23](FLEET-STATE.md#at-d2-23-a-retired-seats-desk-goes-and-only-an-announcement-removes-it)
tests it at the state layer and
[AT-D3-16](#at-d3-16-retirement-removes-the-desk-and-the-removal-is-explained) is its rendering half.
Both were **rewritten** by this card rather than deleted: an acceptance test that vanishes with the
behaviour it pinned leaves no record that the rule was ever considered.

## 4. The screens

Three screens, one client, one held seat map. The drill-down is a panel over the floor rather than a
route of its own, because closing it must not cost a reconnect.

### 4.1 The lobby — the building summary

**Purpose:** which floors exist, whether the building is telling the truth, and where to go — and, since
card#12113, **what on each floor needs a look**, read in the lobby without riding to the floor.

⭐ **THE LOBBY IS A DRAWN ROOM FACING THE ELEVATOR WALL, AND THE FLOORS ARE A DIRECTORY MOUNTED ON THAT
WALL BESIDE THE ELEVATOR — the operator's ruling of 2026-10-20 (card#12113, closing card#11800):** *"Proceed
to implement the latest proposal for G"*, concept G of the second lobby round (*the lobby, with a floor
directory beside the elevator*), with the two readings the operator gave with it — *"the lobby elevator
should work when clicked on it, just like the other floors"* and *"When the elevator door opens at the
Lobby, we should see the building front door and windows (from an interior view)"*. It **supersedes the
building cross-section** this section, [§ 10.4](#104-the-art-direction-as-a-specification) and
[decision 37](#13-decisions-taken-revisable-at-review)'s premise drew the lobby as from card#7343 to this
card: no plate, no shaft, no cab gliding between storeys, no roof and no ground lobby, and **no
cab-position indicator of any kind** — not the cue on a plate, not a sign over the door, not a car drawn
in a shaft — because the lobby's elevator is now [§ 4.5](#45-the-viewport-rule-and-the-camera)'s ride and
a ride is navigation, which [§ 4.5](#45-the-viewport-rule-and-the-camera) says is never state. **What the
ruling does NOT move is this table's sources**: every reading is still computed over the seat objects the
client already holds for the floor's rooms ([§ 2.1](#21-the-seven-values-the-client-computes-about-a-seat-or-about-itself-closed)
row 5), the fleet totals are still read from the wire and never recounted, the discrepancy check still
compares the two ([AT-D3-15](#at-d3-15-the-lobby-never-invents-a-count)), and the layout still adds a
composition and no count. What changed is the **rendering** — a plaque per floor carrying more of what
the client already holds, plus **one member D2 publishes for it**, `longest_open_call`
([D2 § 8.2.1](FLEET-STATE.md#821-the-seat-state-object), card#12113: the oldest open call, which `action`,
the newest, cannot stand in for) — and the table below states each new row's derivation so that no
figure on a plaque is one the client invented. Per-agent detail — the card, the action, the context bar — stays the
floor's ([§ 4.2](#42-the-floor)); the plaque names the agent that needs a look and sends the viewer
there.

| Element | Source | Rendered as |
|---|---|---|
| floor list | the **building layout** ([§ 4.6](#46-the-building-layout)) composed against `installs[].install_id` from the snapshot: every floor the layout declares, plus one floor per install the layout does not place, floor ids ascending | **one plaque per floor on the directory board**, in that order, top to bottom; the plaque's **header** is the floor's name — **its label when the layout gives it one, else its key** ([§ 4.6](#46-the-building-layout), card#9273 — the key is honest and no placeholder is invented) — as the plaque's **one link**, to `/floor/{key}` (the key either way). A floor of more than one room names its rooms on the header's name row — *rooms: kanban, kanban-bridge*, each by its `install_id` alone, **with no form suffix** (the form is the floor page's) — so a viewer can see which installs a floor holds without riding to it, and a room the fleet reports no seat for is marked as such in [§ 4.6](#46-the-building-layout)'s words. ⚠ Until card#12113 this read *one row per floor, the row being the link*, then *one plate per floor*; the plaque is the row's third rendering and reads the same members |
| per-floor state summary — the plaque's **state tally** | the seat objects the client holds for **every install the floor's rooms name** ([§ 2.1](#21-the-seven-values-the-client-computes-about-a-seat-or-about-itself-closed) row 5); a room the fleet reports no seat for contributes none and is named as such ([§ 4.6](#46-the-building-layout)) | one **chip** per `render_state` member present, each carrying its count and the member's word — *2 working*, *1 idle*, *1 stale* — in [§ 7.1](#71-the-render-per-state)'s fixed member order, and after them one chip per unrecognised value the floor holds, carrying the raw string ([§ 5.4](#54-what-is-never-rendered)) exactly as the text line did since card#7943. The chips are the header's **second row**, under the name row. A chip's fill is its member's `--state-<member>` token with a **1 px outline** in the plaque's ink at low opacity — so a pale fill (`stale` on the cream face) keeps its edge — and its word is always on it ([§ 10.4](#104-the-art-direction-as-a-specification)'s palette bullet; colour never carries the state alone, [§ 4.5](#45-the-viewport-rule-and-the-camera)); the plaque's face joins `tools/design/state-chip-colours.py`'s checked surfaces, so the fills are held apart as drawn on it as they are on the floor's. **The text form survives as the header link's accessible name** — *Floor 2, 2 working · 1 idle*, *no seats held* where the plaque holds none — so a screen reader hears what the chips show. ⚠ Until card#12113 this was one text line, *2 working · 1 idle · 1 stale*; the chips are that line's members, one per chip, and the derivation (`lobby-model.js`'s `floorSummary()`) is unchanged |
| the plaque's **agents and desks** (card#12113) | `render_state` over the same seats | *3 agents · 4 desks*, right-aligned on the header's name row, each noun agreeing with its count — *1 agent · 1 desk*. **Desks** is the seats the client holds for the floor's rooms — the held count [AT-D3-15](#at-d3-15-the-lobby-never-invents-a-count) labels, which the discrepancy row below sums. **Agents** is the subset whose `render_state` draws a **character** — `desk/task-bubble.js`'s `deskDrawsCharacter()`, which is true of a *recognised* member ([§ 7.1](#71-the-render-per-state)'s ten) outside that module's `NO_CHARACTER_STATES`, the one shipped statement of that section's Desk column, called and never re-implemented — so an empty chair (`stale`, `offline`) is a desk with nobody at it, and an unrecognised `render_state` counts as a desk and not as an agent, because a character it draws is a claim the client cannot make. Both are counts of what the client **holds**, labelled so on the board's title line. ⚠ A **seat ruling**, revisable: the operator asked for *agent count and desk count* without saying what tells them apart, and the lobby holds no room map, so a map's slot count was not available to be the desk count — [§ 14](#14-open-questions-for-the-review-loop) item 39 |
| the plaque's **marker row** (card#12113) | `render_state` and `seat_id` of each seat the floor's rooms hold | one small marker per held seat, in the floor's rooms' key order and inside a room by `seat_id` ([§ 2.1](#21-the-seven-values-the-client-computes-about-a-seat-or-about-itself-closed) row 6's order for a floor the lobby holds no map for — a desk's slot is the floor screen's computation and the lobby does not run it); filled with the member's `--state-<member>` token under the chips' 1 px outline, drawn as a **disc** for a member that draws a character and as a **ring** for one that draws an empty chair (`NO_CHARACTER_STATES` again), and an unrecognised value as a ring in the sheet's `--state-ink-unconfirmed`; its accessible name is the seat's `seat_id`, a comma and the state's word — on a floor of more than one room the `install_id`, a slash and the `seat_id`, as the attention line names a seat there, since a `seat_id` is unique within one install only — so the colour is never the only carrier. **The first 12 markers in that order, then one tag *+N more*** where N is the held count less 12 ([§ 12](#12-every-number-and-where-it-comes-from)'s *Directory marker cap*) — N is derived from the two counts above and never a third count. ⚠ Lightness, not hue alone, is what tells two markers apart: the fills are the state chip's tokens, held apart as drawn by `tools/design/state-chip-colours.py`'s bound (card#11218, [§ 12](#12-every-number-and-where-it-comes-from)'s *State chip bound*), which the directory adds its plaque face to as one more surface the tool measures over |
| the plaque's **attention line** (card#12113) | `render_state`, `link_state`, `install_id`, `seat_id`; `blocked_since`; `api_error_type` and `activity.last_received_at`; `context.used_pct`; `longest_open_call.tool_name` and `longest_open_call.started_received_at` | **names only what needs a look, and is absent when nothing does** — never *all quiet*, which would be a claim over seats the client may not confirm. Up to three parts in this order, **each on a row of its own** — never one joined line cut at the plaque's edge; the plaque grows by a row per part, and a part wider than the plaque wraps onto further lines of its own row rather than being cut ([§ 4.1](#41-the-lobby--the-building-summary)'s *every line is read whole*) — each opening with the seat's `seat_id` — prefixed by its room, *`install_id`/`seat_id`*, on a floor of more than one room, because a `seat_id` is unique within one install and nowhere else ([D2 § 8.2.1](FLEET-STATE.md#821-the-seat-state-object)): **(a) the agent blocked or stalled longest** — among the floor's seats whose `render_state` is `blocked`, the one with the **earliest `blocked_since`**, rendered *`seat_id` — waiting on a human since 14:31 (seat clock)*: the member is a **seat-clock narrative timestamp** ([D2 § 8.2.1](FLEET-STATE.md#821-the-seat-state-object)), so the ordering is a comparison of the seats' own claims, never an age ([§ 2.4](#24-the-clock-and-every-age-on-the-page)), and the line says so with *(seat clock)*; only where no seat is `blocked`, among those whose `render_state` is `stalled` the one with the **earliest `activity.last_received_at`** (server clock; a null one is excluded, never read as oldest), rendered *`seat_id` — API error — rate_limit (rate limit) — nothing done for 11m*: the error is [§ 7.6](#76-the-three-remaining-member-sets-published-so-membership-is-testable)'s composed line, by reference — the raw `api_error_type` first and verbatim, then its phrase in parentheses, *unrecognised* for a member outside the published set, and the whole composed part omitted on the null `api_error_type` [D2 § 8.2.1](FLEET-STATE.md#821-the-seat-state-object) says a `stalled` seat never carries, as [§ 5.6](#56-the-null-render-for-every-nullable-member) draws the null — followed by the quiet age in [§ 2.4](#24-the-clock-and-every-age-on-the-page)'s form; `blocked` is asked first because [D2 § 4.3](FLEET-STATE.md#43-the-derivation-function) ranks it above `stalled`. **(b) context above the threshold** — among the floor's `live` seats whose `context` is **non-null**, those with `context.used_pct` at or above 80 ([§ 12](#12-every-number-and-where-it-comes-from)'s *Context attention threshold*); the highest is named, *`seat_id` — context 91.2 %*, the figure the wire's own one-decimal `used_pct`. A null `context` is **excluded** — never read as 0, never compared, and never dereferenced ([§ 5.6](#56-the-null-render-for-every-nullable-member)). **(c) a call running unusually long** — among the floor's `live` seats whose **`longest_open_call`** is non-null ([D2 § 8.2.1](FLEET-STATE.md#821-the-seat-state-object), card#12113: the OLDEST open call, published because `action` is the newest and an intern's call replaces a dispatch there while the dispatch stays open — [D2 § 10](FLEET-STATE.md#10-worked-example-the-clear-trace-folded-end-to-end) E3), those whose `longest_open_call.started_received_at` lies 10 minutes or more before the corrected clock ([§ 12](#12-every-number-and-where-it-comes-from)'s *Long-call threshold*; both ends server clock); the longest is named, *`seat_id` — Agent running for 40m 12s*, the tool `longest_open_call.tool_name` and the age in [§ 2.4](#24-the-clock-and-every-age-on-the-page)'s **action-elapsed** wording — the third of that section's four — ticking on [§ 2.5](#25-what-re-renders-and-when)'s 1 s tick, the threshold re-asked with it. **Never `action`**: a plaque reading `action.started_received_at` sees a seconds-old intern call over an hour-old dispatch, and would miss exactly the call the operator asked about. (b) and (c) read **`live` seats only** (`link_state`): the attention line is a claim about **now**, and a dark seat's sample and open call are history under [§ 7.3](#73-currency-labels-what-a-non-live-desk-may-claim)'s currency label; (a) needs no such filter because [D2 § 4.2](FLEET-STATE.md#42-render-precedence) masks a non-`live` seat's activity behind its link state — a `stale` seat whose `activity_state` is `blocked` renders `stale` and is named by no part. The totals row below takes the other rule, and the two are one principle ([§ 14](#14-open-questions-for-the-review-loop) item 39(11)): a **count** is over what is held, a claim about **now** is over what is live. Ties break on the lower `(install_id, seat_id)`. The thresholds are **seat rulings**, revisable at [§ 12](#12-every-number-and-where-it-comes-from)'s two rows |
| the plaque's **floor totals** (card#12113) | `task.ref`; `open_calls`; `subagents_open`; `activity.last_received_at` | *2 cards · 3 open calls · 2 interns · last activity 12s ago*, one row, each noun agreeing with its count — *1 card · 1 open call · 1 intern*. **Cards in hand**: the number of **distinct non-null `task.ref`** values across the floor's held seats — a card two seats hold is one card, and a `task` that is null or whose `ref` is null contributes none (a telemetry title is not a card; [§ 5.6](#56-the-null-render-for-every-nullable-member)). **Open calls**: the sum of `open_calls` over the floor's held seats — the wire's own integer per seat, never a count of `action` objects. **Interns running**: the sum of `subagents_open`, never `subagents[].length`, which is capped ([§ 8](#8-interns--subagent-rendering-and-the-cap), [§ 2.1](#21-the-seven-values-the-client-computes-about-a-seat-or-about-itself-closed)'s forbidden list). **Last activity**: the **latest `activity.last_received_at`** across the floor's held seats, rendered as an age in [§ 2.4](#24-the-clock-and-every-age-on-the-page)'s format with this row's wording, *last activity 12s ago*, ticking; where every seat's is null the part reads *no activity yet*, never *0s* — a sibling of the desk's *nothing done yet*. **Every held seat counts, dark or live**: the totals are a count of the picture the client holds, labelled so on the board's title, and a `stale` seat's card is still a card the floor holds — where the attention line above reads live seats only because it claims something about now (one principle, two rules; [§ 14](#14-open-questions-for-the-review-loop) item 39(11)). The three sums are sums of **held** objects' members, which is what keeps them under [§ 2.1](#21-the-seven-values-the-client-computes-about-a-seat-or-about-itself-closed) row 5 rather than the forbidden list: none of them stands in for a fleet-wide number the wire carries |
| fleet totals | `fleet.seats_total`, `fleet.seats_live` | *4 seats · 4 live*, read from the wire and **never recounted** |
| the discrepancy check | the two above | ⭐ **The trigger is the client protocol's, and this row is its render** (card#7341 step 3): the protocol compares the seats it holds with `fleet.seats_total` on each `fleet{}` [§ 2.1](#21-the-seven-values-the-client-computes-about-a-seat-or-about-itself-closed)'s filter admits, spends the budget below and issues the fetch; the lobby renders the words. When `Σ floors ≠ fleet.seats_total` the lobby renders the disagreement in the floor's own nouns — *showing N of M desks — one desk could not be read* when N < M, and *showing N desks — the building lists M* when N > M. Both sentences are the operator's ratified wording (card#7341, 2026-09-15), quoted here at the counts they were ratified at: *"showing 4 of 5 desks — one desk could not be read"* and *"showing 5 desks — the building lists 4"*; where the shortfall is larger than one desk, the ending's own count agrees with it (*two desks could not be read*). The general rule is the operator's too (card#7341, 2026-09-25): the ending spells its count in words up to nine and in digits past it (*two desks could not be read*, *11 desks could not be read*), and every *desk* agrees with the number it follows (*showing 0 of 1 desk*, *showing 1 desk — the building lists 0*). Neither sentence uses *client* or *fleet* — the protocol's nouns, which name nothing a viewer of this floor is looking at — and neither claims a refresh. The N > M direction is reachable: a client that **missed the `seat.retired` announcement** — it was disconnected when the act ran, or the message was lost — still holds a desk that [§ 3.5](#35-retirement-and-the-only-removal) has already taken off every connected floor and that `seats_total` has already stopped counting. It triggers **one snapshot fetch per distinct (N, M) observation**: a disagreement still standing after that fetch is rendered and **not** re-fetched, so a discrepancy the snapshot cannot resolve costs one request rather than one every 15 s. **The *refreshing* wording is honest only while a check for the exact `(N, M)` pair can still run** — while one is in flight, or the pair is unspent and the client is live. Once the one check that pair will ever get (absent a refund) has run and not resolved the disagreement, with no refund due and no discovery still in flight for it, the words must stop claiming an ongoing refresh — and so must they once no check can EVER run for it, because the initial snapshot itself failed and the client has not been re-run: that desk already carries [§ 9](#9-failure-paths-and-their-observables)'s failure render, so this line does not need a wording of its own for that case, only silence. **Neither of the two sentences above claims a refresh** — the wording the operator ratified (card#7341, 2026-09-15) makes no such claim in either direction — so the ordinary checked-once-but-unresolved case needs no second string of its own: the same words are honest whether the one check this pair gets is still to come or has already run without resolving it. What stays conditional is the silence. It never silently picks a winner ([AT-D3-15](#at-d3-15-the-lobby-never-invents-a-count)), and it is how a new install is **discovered** — and that fetch **admits** every install it discovers: its rows are applied under [§ 2.2](#22-connect-snapshot-deltas)'s version rule, so no second fetch follows it ([§ 2.3](#23-membership-a-seat-or-an-install-the-client-does-not-hold) row 3, [decision 9](#13-decisions-taken-revisable-at-review)). A fetch that **fails** — a non-2xx, no response, or a `200` whose body is not a JSON object — spends nothing, so the next heartbeat retries the same `(N, M)`; and one such fetch is in flight at a time, a `fleet{}` admitted meanwhile being evaluated when it ends |
| membership age | the time of the last full snapshot | *membership as of 14:23:14* ([§ 2.3](#23-membership-a-seat-or-an-install-the-client-does-not-hold)) |
| store / derivation / sweep | `fleet.db`, `fleet.fold`, `fleet.sweep`, `fleet.max_fold_lag_ms`, `fleet.sweep_last_run_at`, `fleet.ingest_last_receipt_at` | three separate indicators, never one aggregate — [D2 § 8.2.4](FLEET-STATE.md#824-the-fleet-health-object): "no aggregate rolls three health facts into one… D3 may compose a banner from these three; the wire keeps them apart" |
| feed status | the client's own connection state ([§ 9](#9-failure-paths-and-their-observables)) | *live* · *polling (feed down)* · *reconnecting* · *reload required*, with the resync count beside it |
| the event log | the client's own record ([§ 5.5](#55-the-clients-own-narration)), newest first, capped at 200 lines | text only. **The lobby is a renderer of that record and not its home** — § 5.5 owns what the record is and what goes into it; what this row states is that the lobby is where it is read, so a desk that moved, appeared or vanished has a written cause somebody can find |

⭐ **THE DIRECTORY IS THE LAYOUT'S, NOT `installs[]`' — card#9267.** The lobby listed one plaque per
install because a floor *was* an install; under the room model it lists the floors
[§ 4.6](#46-the-building-layout) composes, and an install the layout does not place still gets a
floor of its own, so **the directory has a plaque for every install either way and can never have a
hole where a room is.** What did not change is everything below: the summary is still counted over
seats the client already holds, the fleet totals are still read from the wire and never recounted,
the discrepancy check still compares the two, and the plaque's header is still the link. The layout
adds a **composition**, not a source of counts. ⚠ Until card#12113 this paragraph said *plate* and
*stack*; the plaque inherits every property the plate had, and the paragraph's argument is unchanged.

⚠ **Until card#12113 this section read: *The ratified building cross-section is a rendering of this
table, and changes nothing in it* — one floor plate per floor, stacked, an elevator as the way between
them, the plate being the link — built by card#7343 (PR #96, `server/public/js/lobby/building-model.js`,
and [Appendix B](#appendix-b--what-an-implementer-builds-from-this) row 16's two slices: the ride's
arrival and the camera at building scale, then the plates drawn as the reference's section with the cab
in its shaft, the roof sign and the ground lobby).** The operator's ruling of 2026-10-20 replaces that
rendering with the room below. Two things the cross-section paragraph argued survive it unchanged and are
restated here because the room rests on them too: **the lobby still draws no desk** — a lobby that drew
the desks themselves would make its counts a thing a viewer counts by eye, and
[AT-D3-15](#at-d3-15-the-lobby-never-invents-a-count) exists because counting by eye is where an invented
count comes from — and **[§ 4.4](#44-routes-and-what-each-one-fetches)'s routes are untouched**: the way
to a floor is still the floor's own route, reached by the plaque's link or by the elevator's ride.

**The room, the directory and the elevator — what is drawn, where, and from what (card#12113).** The
lobby is drawn as **one room seen from inside, standing in it and facing the elevator wall**, in a
one-point perspective — the convention the cab's interior and the view through its doors already use
([§ 4.5](#45-the-viewport-rule-and-the-camera)'s *cab's look*, [§ 10.4](#104-the-art-direction-as-a-specification)'s
projection bullet names the two conventions and where each holds). The drawing is a scene of
**1,440 × 772** scene px ([§ 12](#12-every-number-and-where-it-comes-from)'s *Lobby room drawing*),
under [§ 4.5](#45-the-viewport-rule-and-the-camera)'s camera exactly as the cross-section was — fit on
entry, every gesture, key and zoom button the floor's, the whole-room control where the whole-building
control stood (the page's framing control, *Fit the lobby*) — and it is **scenery carrying no fact**: it
reads no plate's key, no seat and no count, so two buildings of any two shapes draw one room, and its
only words are the sign's. Its parts, each in the drawing's own figures (which carry
no fact and are not [§ 12](#12-every-number-and-where-it-comes-from) rows — the room's scene size is):

- **The room.** The far wall is the elevator wall, a rectangle of the lobby palette's wall ink standing in
  the middle of the scene (its corners at about 273 and 1,166 across, 187 and 666 down); the ceiling
  above it and the floor below it recede from the scene's edges to that wall, the floor in boards of
  the palette's floor and plank inks converging on the wall, the side walls either side in the wall ink
  with a shading toward the far wall, a rail along all three walls, a skirting along their foot, **the
  ceiling's lights as an evenly spaced grid of rectangular recessed panels** — the operator's request of
  2026-10-20, verbatim: *"the ceiling light pattern in the lobby as well as from the elevator cab view is
  not realistic. there should be evenly spaced rectangular lights in a grid pattern"* — **4 across × 3
  deep** ([§ 12](#12-every-number-and-where-it-comes-from)'s *Lobby room drawing* row, a seat ruling from
  the reference drawing): the ceiling trapezoid divided into four bays of 360 scene units across with a
  200-unit panel centred in each, and three equal bays in depth, panels and gaps alike foreshortened
  toward the ceiling's vanishing point at (720, 492.5), each panel in the lamp ink with its soft glow —
  and the four room edges drawn as faint lines. On the left wall a bench; in the back right corner a potted plant; on the right wall a framed
  picture of a hill under a sun, in the drawing's own inks — and **on the left wall one window**, carrying
  the sky as the sky paragraph below says. The palette is
  `building-scene.js`'s `INK` constants — the same wall, floor, plank, skirting, slab, door, door-edge,
  lamp, sign, leaf, pot and mat inks the cross-section drew with, so nothing is re-coloured — plus the
  board's two wood tones and a shading ink, which are the drawing's own.
- **The elevator**, right of the wall's centre: a frame in the board's honey tone round a dark recess, two
  leaves in the building's door colours (`INK.door` / `INK.doorEdge`, held equal to the sheet's
  `--door` / `--door-edge`, [§ 10.4](#104-the-art-direction-as-a-specification)), a lamp arc over the
  doors, a sill, a mat before them, and a two-button call plate beside the frame; over the door the
  brass sign reading the building's name. **It is a CONTROL and nothing else on the wall is**: the
  elevator's leaves and its surround are one button — `role="button"`, in the tab order, named *the
  elevator — ride to another floor*, pressed by a click, Enter or Space, `aria-disabled` while a ride is
  in flight, refusing a press then — exactly the floor's drawn elevator
  ([§ 4.5](#45-the-viewport-rule-and-the-camera)'s floor's ride, card#11795), through the same code
  path: a press is the lobby screen's `ride()`, and what follows is the ride [§ 4.5](#45-the-viewport-rule-and-the-camera)
  states once for both pages. **Behind its leaves is the cab**: `floor/cab-paint.js`'s `drawCabInterior()`
  from the landing's eye (`LANDING`), clipped to the doorway, as the floor's band draws it, so a ride
  arriving at the lobby — its leaves drawn open and closing — shows the cab the viewer just stepped out
  of. **No cab-position indicator**: no cue, no *at:* sign, no dial reading a floor — the sign over the
  door is the building's name, the dial over the cab's own door inside is plain
  ([§ 4.5](#45-the-viewport-rule-and-the-camera)), and the cab's leaves on the lobby's wall move only
  with the viewer's own ride. The keyboard's focus on the elevator outside the camera's view brings the
  camera to it, as focus on a plate did (the lobby screen's `focusElevator()`, `focusOn()` over the elevator's rect),
  and a press focuses it too.
- **The directory board**, left of the elevator on the same wall: a wooden board — a honey face with a
  darker inset and four brass fixings — and inside it **the directory**, whose title line reads ***FLOOR
  DIRECTORY — counts the seats this client holds*** (the label [AT-D3-15](#at-d3-15-the-lobby-never-invents-a-count)
  requires, moved from the floors heading the cross-section stood under): the title is **HTML in the
  directory's own counter-scaled layer**, the heading the directory list is `aria-labelledby`, and never
  a word painted into the drawn board — the drawing carries no fact, and this line is one: the plaques
  of the table above, one per floor, each a cream plaque with a soft frame, laid out as **rows, one under
  another, each read whole** (the final drawing, `docs/design/lobby-preview/Lobby2G.dc.html`, is the worked
  example at the board's width): the header's **name row** — a numeral in the sign's ink with the plaque's
  index in the list, the floor's name as the link, the room names where the plaque names any, and the
  agents-and-desks figures right-aligned; the header's **tally row** — the state chips; the **marker row**;
  **one row per attention part** where there is any; and the **totals row**. **Under the board** stand the
  building's own readings as two brass-edged panels: the left one *Building readings* — **each reading
  on a line of its own**: the feed status, its resync count, the fleet totals, the three indicators, the
  ingest line and the membership stamp, and the discrepancy sentence where there is one; the right
  one the client's event log, newest first, under the heading ***Event log***. Every one of those is this
  table's row, unchanged in source and wording; the board moves where they stand and not what they say.
- **The directory's text is at the page's own text size and is never scaled by the camera** —
  [decision 37](#13-decisions-taken-revisable-at-review) holds for the plaque exactly as it held for the
  plate, and for the same reason: the lobby exists to pick a floor, so a floor's name and what needs a
  look on it are read before any zoom. **The directory is drawn in the camera's layer, so it stays on
  the board at every zoom and pan** — its box is the board's inner rectangle in scene px — and its text
  is counter-scaled to `1rem` inside that box, the one writer being the lobby page's camera hook (the
  successor of the plate's, called on every camera the page shows and never from a render). When the
  plaques are taller than the box at the camera's zoom, **the directory scrolls inside its box**
  (`overflow-y: auto`), and **a pan gesture that begins over it — a wheel, or a one-finger or primary-button
  drag — is the directory's while the directory can still move the gesture's way, and the camera's
  otherwise** — the edge rule [§ 4.5](#45-the-viewport-rule-and-the-camera) already states for the drawing's
  own edge, applied one level in (`wire/camera-gestures.js`, over an element that declares it scrolls;
  the floor's drawing declares none and is untouched): a wheel notch is asked of the directory first and
  handed to the camera when the directory is at its end that way; a drag decides at its first move, from
  the element it began over and the direction it moves, and keeps that owner until it ends, so a drag
  never flips from scrolling the list to panning the room half-way. **The directory is `touch-action: none`
  like the drawing around it**, and the gesture wire drives its scroll itself from the drag it owns —
  because a scroll container inside a `touch-action: none` ancestor does not inherit that value (Pointer
  Events Level 3 § 8.2 resolves `touch-action` per element), so a directory left at `auto` would have the
  browser scroll it natively and cancel the pointer stream the hand-off reads, and the edge hand-off above
  would never fire. The keyboard's focus on a plaque's
  link scrolls the directory to it — the browser's own scroll-into-view inside the directory's box — and
  brings the camera to the board where the board is not wholly in view (the lobby screen's `focusBoard()`,
  `focusOn()` over the board's rect, as a plate's focus moved the camera). **Every line is read whole**:
  a line wider than its box wraps onto further lines — breaking inside a word only where the word alone
  is wider — so a plaque grows taller rather than hiding a figure, and the board's title, the totals row
  and each reading wrap the same way. **On the name row the floor's name and the agents and desks never
  shrink; the rooms line is the one part that gives way**, taking what the row has left beside them and
  wrapping inside it, and where the name and the figures do not fit side by side the figures move to a
  line of their own, still right-aligned. ⚠ **One residual, declared:** at a phone's width the fitted
  board's box holds less than one plaque at `1rem`, so the directory scrolls almost at once — the plate's
  phone-width residual, inherited ([§ 14](#14-open-questions-for-the-review-loop) item 39); and there,
  where the board's face is narrower than [§ 12](#12-every-number-and-where-it-comes-from)'s *Directory
  title wrap width*, the title is one line cut at its end, because a title wrapped there would fill the
  box and leave the plaques none. The drag hand-off is measured in a headless
  browser with synthetic pointers, as the camera's gestures are — and synthetic pointers **bypass
  `touch-action`**, so that measurement cannot see the native-scroll cancellation the rule exists to avoid:
  **the touch half is declared unverified until a real device has run it**, and stays so in item 39(4).
- ⭐ **At a phone's or a tablet's width the directory leaves the board and DOCKS under the room — the
  operator's request of 2026-10-22 (card#12187): *"the lobby directory is unreadable on a phone without
  zooming"*, with the room's board left as it is on the desktop and laptop surfaces card#12113 measured.** The
  board's box is a fixed share of the room — its inner rectangle is 488 of the room's 1,440 scene px across and
  308 of 772 down — so at fit its face is that share of the surface: on a phone of 360–430 CSS px the surface is
  344–414 px wide after the section's 8 px margins, so the face is 117–140 px wide and 74–88 px tall, which
  holds a fraction of one plaque at `1rem` (**B**'s 390 × 700 run at fit, read on the shipped build on
  2026-10-22: a list 1,230 px tall in a scroller 49 px tall), and the board view the camera can bring it to is
  366 × 231 px holding one plaque with the readings off the screen. No counter-scale makes a 117 px box read, so
  **below a bound the lobby stops standing the directory on the board**: docked, the directory's box and the
  readings' box stand in the page's own flow under the drawing surface — the directory first, the full width of
  the section, then the two readings panels stacked one under the other — at the page's text size with no
  counter-scale, the plaques' list no scroller of its own, and the page scrolled by the browser. The room stays
  drawn above them at fit — its board an empty honey face, the directory now under the room: on a laptop-height
  viewport (1,366 × 657, the surface capped at 80 vh, 526 px tall, under the page's header) the first screen shows
  the room and its empty board, and the directory stands below the fold, reached by scrolling the page (review F6) — with its elevator still the one control (its surround is 193 × 294 scene px,
  46 × 70 CSS px at a 344 px surface's fit), its window still A17's, and the camera's keys, buttons and *Fit the
  lobby* as they are.
  **The bound is CHOSEN, and it is a size of the fitted face, not of the window**: the lobby docks when the
  directory's face at the room's fit — the camera's fit zoom, `min(surface.w / extent.w, surface.h / extent.h)`,
  times the box's 488 × 308 scene px — is narrower than **24 em** or shorter than **15 em**, which at a 16 px
  rem is a surface narrower than 1,133 CSS px or shorter than 608 — the width figure binds first on a short
  surface too, because the box's 488 : 308 is narrower than 24 : 15, so a face 15 em tall is already under 24 em
  wide ([§ 12](#12-every-number-and-where-it-comes-from)'s *Directory dock width*, which carries the measurement it
  rests on). It is chosen rather than derived from a readability target because the target the review asked
  for — the title and one whole plaque inside the fitted face — is not met by the desktop board card#12113
  shipped either: **B**'s fit runs over the attention fixture hold 1.22 of its tallest plaque at a 1,440 × 900
  viewport, 0.95 at 1,280 × 800 and 0.81 at 1,366 × 768, scrolling the rest. The bound is drawn under the
  1,366 × 768 *viewport* — and **a real laptop's page viewport is shorter than its screen**: a browser's tab and
  address bars take 80–110 px, so a 1,366 × 768 laptop shows about 1,366 × 657 and a 1,280 × 800 one about
  1,280 × 690, where the surface's 80 vh cap makes the fit height-limited and the face shorter than 15 em. **Those
  laptops dock, and that is the ruling** (the seat's, on round 2's N3, revisable, recorded in decision 72): the
  docked layout is the readable one — the directory the section's full width at the page's text size — so
  docking the laptop serves the request more than keeping the board does. What stays on the board is the
  surface tall enough for a 1,440-wide face of 15 em: a window about 1,440 × 760 or taller (**24.6 × 15.6 em** at 1,440 × 780, which **B** runs). It
  is re-asked on every resize **and on every change of the page's text size** (a change the browser fires no
  `resize` for: the docking entry observes a `1rem` probe with a `ResizeObserver`, so an `em` bound never goes
  stale), and the boxes move back onto the board when the face grows past it — the one move that drops a
  keyboard's focus on a plaque, named in [§ 14](#14-open-questions-for-the-review-loop) item 39(4).
  **What docks is the DOM, and ONE entry writes every state the dock changes** — `lobby/directory.js`'s
  docking entry (canon #5: one writer, so no second module derives the predicate). The two boxes live in the
  page markup after the surface and are moved into the camera's layer only while the room is drawn and the face
  is not under the bound; the move is made only when the box's parent is not already the right one, so a render
  and the 1 s tick move nothing. With the move the entry writes **`data-home` on each box — `board`, `dock` or
  `flow`** — and **the surface's `touch-action`**. **The markup ships `data-home="flow"` on both boxes** (the
  Blade page, `dashboard.blade.php`'s boxes), so the placeholder *waiting for the fleet snapshot* is styled for
  the page's ground from the first paint and with no script run, rather than from a state only the module
  writes — the entry's one job at load is to move a box OUT of `flow` once a room is drawn, and back when it is
  not (round 2's N6). Every style that depends on where a box stands is keyed on the box's own `data-home` and
  never on an ancestor it may leave: the un-drawn placeholder colours that card#12113 keyed on
  `#lobby-room:not([data-drawn])` move to `[data-home="flow"]` (on the layer they read nothing once the boxes
  stand outside it, and the placeholder would be the board's dark plaque ink on the page's dark ground,
  ≈ 1.3 : 1 — review round 1's F2), and `building-scene.js`'s `surfaceStyle()` stops writing `touchAction`,
  which the entry now owns (review round 1's F9).
  **The camera's surface is the surface as the room is drawn in it, measured even while the room is not drawn**
  (card#12319). With the boxes in the page's flow the un-drawn surface holds only the empty camera's layer and
  measures zero high at every window size, a surface `wire/camera.js` refuses; `lobby/main.js`'s `surface()`
  measures it under `surfaceStyle()`'s drawn style and puts the un-drawn style back in the same synchronous call,
  so the screen's camera starts, and the stream opens, before the first snapshot. A lobby whose script cannot
  start says *the lobby could not start — <cause>; reload the page to try again* in the building readings and
  the directory, in place of their *waiting* placeholders (`lobby-model.js`'s `startFailure()`), and the error
  still reaches the console. `Tests\Feature\Lobby\TheLobbyStartsBeforeItsRoomIsDrawnTest` holds both over the
  page's own script, with a planted control for each; `tools/design/floor-ride.browser.mjs`'s lobby rows load
  the served page in headless Chromium.
  **`touch-action` is `none` ONLY where the wire listens, and `auto` everywhere else — the primitive inverted**
  (round 2's N2 and N5). The one primitive is a rule keyed on `data-home`: **`none` under
  `[data-home="board"]`** for the list and the two readings panels, and **`none` on the surface only while a
  box is on the board** (the entry writes it), because the wire reads those drags and a native scroll or zoom
  would cancel the pointer stream it hand-off rests on; **`auto` under `dock` and `flow`**, the surface
  included, because the browser, not the wire, owns every touch there. Not `pan-y`: a `pan-y` element refuses
  the browser's pinch-zoom (per round 2's review of Pointer Events 3 § 8.3), which would strip the page's zoom
  from a phone reader — a failure of WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.4 *Resize Text* (Level AA), the one the docked layout
  exists to serve — so no element a docked finger can touch says `none` **or `pan-y`**.
  **Fingers.** Docked, a one-finger drag on the directory, the readings or the page around them scrolls the page
  natively, with the browser's own momentum, and a two-finger pinch zooms the page, because every element from
  the touched one up is `auto` (a browser pans only when each one allows it — review round 1's F1). The gesture
  wire never sees those drags — the boxes stand outside the surface it listens on — so there is no inner scroll
  to hand off and this section's drag hand-off applies on the board alone. The readings' two panels keep a native
  inner scroll each, capped at ten of their lines, so a 200-line event log does not stand ten screens tall, and
  a finger scrolls that panel and then, at its end, the page. **The docked room is the browser's too**: its
  surface is `auto`, so on touch a drag or pinch that begins on the drawing scrolls or zooms the PAGE and the
  wire sees a `pointercancel` (which it already treats as no click) — the room's camera is then driven by its
  zoom buttons, *Fit the lobby* and the keys, and on a mouse or a pen by the wire as ever. That is the cost of
  not stealing the page's zoom; the room is the top quarter of a phone's page (184 px tall at a 344 px surface,
  the room's 1,440 : 772) and nothing on it is read by dragging. (Round 1's `pan-y` rule for the surface is
  withdrawn with the pinch sentence that rested on it: on a `pan-y` surface a two-finger pinch does reach the
  wire — `wire/camera-gestures.js`'s pinch branch reads the second pointer — so the earlier claim that its
  zoom was *unpromised* was wrong in the other direction, and the page's zoom was the casualty.) **Taps.** A
  plaque's floor name is its link and opens its floor, as on the board; docked, the link's box is at least
  **24 × 24 CSS px** (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 *Target Size (Minimum)*, Level AA, read at
  `https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#target-size-minimum` on 2026-10-22 — its *inline* exception would otherwise
  excuse a link in a line of text, so the floor is declared rather than relied on), by a minimum height on the
  link under `[data-home="dock"]` and nowhere else; the elevator rides as the floor's does. **The title wraps**
  on a docked face — a phone of 360 px gives it 344 px, 21.5 em — and no board face is under 24 em, so the
  one-line cut the board's phone face needed is retired with the container rule that made it, and no figure of
  the directory is cut at any width (claim 10 below, with no residual). ⚠ **The touch half stays declared until
  a real phone has run it** — synthetic pointers bypass `touch-action`, as above, which is why claim 14 reads the
  COMPUTED `touch-action` of everything a docked finger can touch rather than driving a finger — and the
  operator's own phone is where the card asks for it to be run (item 39(4)).
- **Under [§ 9](#9-failure-paths-and-their-observables) F17** — no layout held — the room and its board
  are drawn once a full snapshot has applied (the room carries no fact), and the directory lists the
  snapshot's installs as F17 says, each a plain link *`install_id` — no floor claimed* with no plaque
  figures, under the F17 statement; the elevator's cab then offers *Lobby* alone, a stay, because no
  floor is composed to ride to. Before a snapshot has applied nothing is drawn and the page's
  placeholders stand, as before this card.

**What a reviewer should check this against, named:** the plaque reads no member the table does not
name; the directory, the room and the elevator are three elements and the room's is the only drawing;
the cab's leaves on the wall move with the ride and with nothing else; and the sky's one driver is the
window's (below).

⚠ **Until card#12113 the numbered claims here were the PLATE's label contract** — its text read at the body size beside
the building or on its plate, a counter-scale, a side, a line budget against a storey, a backing and a halo, the cab's
cue — held by a test and a hand-run contrast tool that went with the plate. Card#12113's last slice rewrote them into the
directory plaque's contract below, in the same form; what it carries over and what it dropped are the room paragraph's
above, and are not a second copy here.

**The directory plaque.** The directory's text — its title, each plaque's rows and the readings under the board — is read
at the page's own size because the lobby exists to pick a floor before any zoom ([decision 37](#13-decisions-taken-revisable-at-review)).
Each claim below names the check that holds it: **T** is `server/tests/Feature/Lobby/TheLobbyIsADrawnRoomTest.php`, and
**B** is `tools/design/lobby-directory.browser.mjs`, run by hand in headless Chromium over its own `RUNS` (not wired
in CI: `tools/design/README.md`). How each is done is the code's own docblocks'.

1. **Size.** `directory.js`'s `showDirectory()` keeps every text of the directory — the title, a plaque's rows, the
   readings — at `1rem` on the screen at every camera: each is laid out in a face whose font size is `1rem`, sized to its
   box at the camera's zoom and scaled by the zoom's inverse through the two properties `showDirectory()` writes
   (`--lobby-zoom`, `--lobby-scale`). (held by: T::test_green_the_text_is_counter_scaled_by_one_writer_inside_boxes_on_the_board;
   T::test_green_the_directory_scrolls_inside_its_box_and_every_line_reads_whole; B check 'size')
2. **The page's own size.** The lobby page sets no text size on the root, the body, `*` or a tag `directory.js` builds, none with `!important`, and none in a style block or attribute, so `1rem` is the viewer's body text size. (held by: T::test_green_the_lobby_page_sets_no_text_size_of_its_own)
3. **One writer.** `lobby/main.js`'s `view()` — the page's camera hook, called on every camera the page shows — calls
   `showDirectory()`, and none of `paint()`, `paintScene()` and `paintDirectory()` calls it or writes a `--lobby-` property;
   a camera that frames nothing gets no write. (held by:
   `server/tests/Feature/Lobby/LobbyPageWiringTest.php`::test_the_page_wires_the_ride_and_the_rooms_camera_to_the_screen,
   through its `showDirectoryPlacementDefects()`; T::test_green_the_text_is_counter_scaled_by_one_writer_inside_boxes_on_the_board)
4. **The board is the one box.** While the room is drawn the directory's box stands at `building-scene.js`'s `directory`
   rect — the board's inner rectangle — in scene px, clipping its face, and the face fills the box on the screen at every
   camera; with no room drawn neither carries a style. (held by: T::test_green_the_text_is_counter_scaled_by_one_writer_inside_boxes_on_the_board;
   T::test_green_the_room_is_drawn_from_nothing_and_its_only_words_are_the_signs; B check 'board')
5. **It scrolls inside its box — on the board.** The plaques' list is `overflow-y: auto` and `touch-action: none`, and declares
   `data-camera-scrolls`; a long directory holds more than it shows and reaches its last plaque when scrolled to its end.
   Docked (claim 14) the list is no scroller: the page is.
   (held by: T::test_green_the_directory_scrolls_inside_its_box_and_every_line_reads_whole; B check 'scroll')
6. **The hand-off.** A wheel begun over an element that declares it scrolls moves it while it can move the wheel's way and
   the camera once it cannot; a Ctrl+wheel there is the camera's zoom; a drag decides its owner at its first move and keeps
   it, and a drag that scrolled is no click. (held by:
   `server/tests/Feature/Floor/TheCameraWireIsOneForBothPagesTest.php`::test_green_a_gesture_over_a_scroller_is_its_own_while_it_can_move)
7. **The touch half.** On the board, a real finger's drag over the directory reaches the gesture wire whole — the browser
   never scrolls the list natively and cancels the pointer stream; docked (claim 14), a finger's drag on the directory, the
   readings or the page scrolls the page natively, a pinch zooms the page, and the room is the browser's on touch
   (`touch-action: auto` everywhere off the board).
   (declared, unchecked: synthetic pointers bypass `touch-action`, so only a real device can show either half — § 14 item 39(4))
8. **The name and the link.** A plaque's one link is its `href` — the key's route — named by its `accessible_name`, the
   floor's name, a comma and the tally's text form. (held by: T::test_green_each_plaque_is_painted_as_the_model_decided_it)
9. **Every row as decided, in order.** The name row (the numeral, the link, the rooms where the plaque names any, the agents
   and desks), the tally row (a chip per member, its member's fill), the marker row (each marker named, then the tag where
   there is one), a row per attention part and none where there is none, and the totals row last — each the model's string.
   (held by: T::test_green_each_plaque_is_painted_as_the_model_decided_it;
   T::test_green_the_unclaimed_and_the_empty_directory_are_said_in_words)
10. **Every line read whole.** A plaque row wraps (`flex-wrap: wrap` on the row, `overflow-wrap: anywhere` on the face)
    and none of a plaque row, the board's title (but under claim 14's narrow-face rule), the rooms line, the agents and
    desks or a reading is `white-space: nowrap` cut by `text-overflow: ellipsis`; on the name row the name and the agents and desks are `flex: none`, so the rooms line
    is the one part that gives way. In every one of B's `RUNS` no element of the two faces is wider than its box under an
    overflow that is not `visible`, or taller than it under one that only hides — except the `CLIP_RESIDUALS` B declares,
    each by run and element, a list card#12187 empties: the title's one-line cut on the phone's fitted board goes with
    that board (claim 14), and the container rule that cut it is retired. (held by:
    T::test_green_the_directory_scrolls_inside_its_box_and_every_line_reads_whole; B check 'clip')
11. **Focus brings the board — on the board.** The keyboard's focus on a plaque's link with the board not wholly in view
